newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Wednesday's gains to 15,166,7 points but analysts said stronger selling after fixing suggested the market was returning to its downtrend in the run-up to September's parliamentary vote.

"It seems there's no big chance for sharp falls -- 15,000 points has already been tested and held to a degree -- so it in the mid-term the bourse could hover around that line," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Analysts also said the central bank head's statement in a newspaper on Wednesday that she would soon raise nominal interest rates should limit buying.
On Thursday the daily Gazeta Wyborcza quoted unofficial sources as saying the central bank would raise nominal rates on Friday but the bank's press office had no comment.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.9 percent to 15,166.7 points and turnover rose 33.5 percent to 179.9 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts also said recent flooding, seen costing billions of dollars, would dampen buying, although the finance minister said on Wednesday it was unlikely to slow significantly economic growth or create strong inflationary pressure.
Analysts said Optimus, up 9.6 percent in heavy trade after Wednesday's 10-percent surge, continued its apparently speculative rise.

They said Prochnik fell 9.7 percent in light trade after recent big gains as players continued to speculate on whether the stock's price had been illegally manipulated along with others on the parallel market.
The National Investment Fund NIF index rose 2.7 percent to 130.6 points and NFI units rose 3.7 percent to 127 zlotys, extending their rebound after recent falls.
